clue.text: Game by the fireside

definitions.meaning: a card game played for stakes
the iron rod kept at the hearth for stirring the coals

explanation.surface: A cosy evening of cards or board games beside the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a gambling card game and the metal rod used to stir a fire, which lives at the hearth.

clue.text: Rider in mail appears on one animal

parts.note: mail is the post
I is the Roman numeral for one
the lion is the big cat

explanation.surface: A courier who arrives carrying the mail while mounted on some beast.
explanation.walkthrough: A postilion rides the leading horse of a carriage team; 'in' and 'appears on' simply join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A postilion is a horseman who rides one of the horses drawing a coach, so he is a kind of rider.

clue.text: Deceitful fellow found in clubs perhaps

definitions.meaning: the jack, a court card present in each suit such as clubs

explanation.surface: A swindler who hangs around gentlemen's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a dishonest rogue and is also the old name for the jack in a pack of playing cards, which appears in clubs.

clue.text: Beer roughly a pound, wool up and rising

indicators.note: roughly says the letters of the word beer are handled loosely and rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from Latin libra)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for wool is read from bottom to top

parts.note: noil is the short fibre combed out of wool

explanation.surface: A tally of rough beer, a pound of money and some wool, piled high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges BEER to REBE; 'up' turns NOIL into LION.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or revolt against authority, the same as a revolt by the people.

clue.text: Cajoling many into changing direction

indicators.note: into says the letter for many goes inside the word for changing direction

parts.note: wheeling is turning round, as a flock or a column of troops does
D is the Roman numeral 500, taken as a large number

explanation.surface: Persuading a crowd to turn about face.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe coaxing someone with flattery to get one's own way.

clue.text: Little is about to suspend the cane

indicators.note: is about says the word for little surrounds the word for suspend

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
to hang is to suspend

explanation.surface: A small child is about to hang up a walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: A whangee is a cane made from a kind of Chinese bamboo, used for walking sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Whangee is a type of bamboo, and a walking stick made from its stem is a cane.

clue.text: Play seen on board?

parts.note: suggests a drama staged on a ship or on stage boards, but means the final phase of a chess game played on the board

explanation.surface: A theatre performance put on aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing stage of a chess game, played out on the chessboard, is the play seen there at the finish.

clue.text: Was fond of little children

parts.note: describes a doting adult who adored small children, read as the plain past tense of lavishing affection

explanation.surface: Someone who adored small children.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote is to be excessively fond of someone, as grandparents are of little ones.

clue.text: Silly nit! Property may not go as he wished

definitions.text: Silly nit! Property may not go as he wished

indicators.note: silly says the letters of nit are muddled into a new order

parts.note: an estate is the property a person leaves at death

explanation.surface: A scolding for a fool who left no will, so his estate will be shared out against his wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges NIT to INT; the whole clue also describes the person, who dies without a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person dying without having made a valid will has property distributed by law rather than by his wishes.

clue.text: Inexperienced in some degree, naturally

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gently naive person, by nature somewhat so.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is the colour of unripe fruit, so it describes someone raw and untrained.

clue.text: Leading poet embraces love by the seaside

parts.note: a star is the leading performer

indicators.note: embraces says the word for poet holds the letter for love

parts.note: a bard is a poet
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A celebrated poet hugs his beloved during a day at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the seaside' is a playful definition: the right-hand side of a ship, facing the sea as she sails.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the right-hand side of a vessel, wittily called the side of the ship at sea.

clue.text: Knight perhaps could be right

definitions.meaning: Sir, an honour given to a knight, is an example of a rank of address
a legal right of ownership, as in deeds to land

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a knight might be proper.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an honorific such as Sir and a legal claim of ownership to property.

clue.text: Visionary thought to have left

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A dreamer considered to have departed.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means existing only in the imagination, perfect but unreal, much like visionary.

clue.text: Richardson's man sees relative about one

indicators.note: about says the word for relative goes around the letter for one

parts.note: a grandson is a family relative
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man visits a kinsman for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Richardson's 1753 novel is 'Sir Charles Grandison', whose hero is the man meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Charles is the title hero of a novel by Samuel Richardson, the 18th-century English writer.

clue.text: Tend to be lean?

definitions.meaning: to be ... or disposed towards something

explanation.surface: Asking whether one tends to be thin.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to have a tendency and to slope or tilt, so it matches each word.

clue.text: Praised firm getting decoration finished

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A company that finished its decorating was praised for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The Military Medal (MM) is a British gallantry award for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe speaking well of someone or recommending them with approval.

clue.text: How to find the root — of a tooth?

definitions.text: How to find the root — of a tooth?

parts.words: How to find the root — of a tooth?
parts.note: first reads as working out the square root of a number, then as a dentist pulling out a tooth by the root

explanation.surface: A dentist pondering how to get at a molar's root.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics one finds a root this way, and a dentist removes a tooth the same way.

clue.text: Article in rent acts causes storms

indicators.note: in says the article sits between the two other words

parts.note: rent is torn, as of cloth
does means acts or performs
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Legislation on rents provokes violent reactions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tornadoes are violent rotating windstorms, so they are a kind of storm.

clue.text: Attlee's new version some Nazis found insipid

indicators.note: a new version says the letters are rearranged into a fresh form

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: Clement Attlee's account, rewritten, struck some Nazis as dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour prime minister after 1945. 'new version' rearranges ATTLEES plus SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe food or ideas that have no flavour or interest.

clue.text: Number fifty is about a talking bird, so-called

indicators.note: is about here means stands next to, so the letter for fifty sits alongside the bird

parts.note: the mina or myna is a mimicking bird
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Number fifty is a bird that talks, supposedly.
explanation.walkthrough: MINA is a variant spelling of myna, the starling relative that imitates speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something existing in name only, not in reality.

clue.text: Meaningful work

parts.note: sounds like significant labour, but means a book full of meanings, a reference work of words

explanation.surface: A job that gives one a sense of purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary is a reference volume that lists the meanings of words, so it is literally full of meaning.

clue.text: Monotonously stuffy?

parts.note: stuffy means lacking fresh atmosphere, while monotonously hints at lacking a tune, as if without melody

explanation.surface: A room that is boringly close and fusty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking fresh atmosphere, a room is stuffy, and lacking a melody it is tuneless, the musical pun.

clue.text: Music of an old poet

parts.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, the medieval Italian poet

explanation.surface: Songs by a medieval poet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a musical movement or piece played at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Asked too much of public, like Charles I

definitions.meaning: demanded excessive payments or efforts from the people
King Charles I levied heavy taxes such as Ship Money without Parliament

explanation.surface: A ruler who demanded too much from his subjects, as Charles I did.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I of England raised unpopular taxes, notably Ship Money, without Parliament, a grievance leading to the Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: It means burdened with excessive taxes or demands, as Charles I did to his subjects with Ship Money.

clue.text: Animal is all right — a quiet one

parts.note: OK means all right
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A creature is fine, and a calm one at that.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest mammal of central Africa related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Boy takes it up this sort of river

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the whole run of letters is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy carries something up a certain river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LADIT round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A river whose flow rises and falls with the sea's ebb and flood is this kind.

clue.text: Passage overlooked in sermon?

parts.note: suggests a section of text skipped by a preacher, but means the walkway between pews that the pulpit looks down on

explanation.surface: A preacher skipped a bit of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The walkway between church pews is a passage, which the preacher looks down over from the pulpit.

clue.text: Some footballers, are; that is to say, queer

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for namely
rum is old British slang for odd

explanation.surface: Some footballers are, so to speak, peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby forwards bound together form the footballers meant; 'are' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby football, the forwards packed together to contest the ball form this formation.

clue.text: Put on by a theological press chief

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theological degree
ed. is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Staged by a religious newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean joined on or included in addition.

clue.text: NCO cooked food for assembly

indicators.note: cooked says the letters NCO are prepared and altered into a new order

parts.note: a course is a portion of a meal

explanation.surface: A sergeant made dinner for a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people in one place is an assembly or crowd.

clue.text: Laziness of the reviewers Tennyson addressed

definitions.meaning: Tennyson's Hendecasyllabics opens by addressing a chorus of idle, careless reviewers

explanation.surface: Tennyson rebuking lazy critics.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's poem 'Hendecasyllabics' begins 'O you chorus of indolent reviewers'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the quality of being idle and averse to effort, the trait Tennyson attributed to critics.

clue.text: Island's second prophet

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: An island's second holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean.
